UnitStatement: Deliverable DEL-05-04 is the Runtime Replay and Transcript View, in package PKG-05 Session Audit, Replay, and Tool Result Records.
DEL-05-04 is typed as a BACKEND_FEATURE_SLICE under decomposition variant SOFTWARE_DECOMP v3.2.
DEL-05-04 scope items are SOW-042 and SOW-046, against objective OBJ-003.
Anticipated artifacts are a replay parser, transcript reconstruction tests, and malformed-tail tests.
The primary store is `.chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/events.jsonl`, the product-owned Chirality audit mirror.

Session metadata input is `.chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/session.json`, carrying session identity, project root, persona, mode, model, SDK linkage, transcript/store linkage, and resume metadata where available.
Existing legacy `{sessionRoot}/{sessionId}.json` records remain readable during migration.
A `HarnessEvent` record includes schemaVersion, eventId, sessionId, optional turnId, optional parentEventId, timestamp, type, and a data payload.
Replay must ignore malformed trailing JSONL lines while preserving valid prior events and surfacing diagnostics.
Transcript content target is accepted user turns, assistant output, tool summaries, terminal outcomes, artifact links, and SDK transcript links.
SDK transcript paths and store keys are secondary adapter metadata unless explicitly imported into HarnessEvent form.
Browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents are separate contracts; replay must not make public UI/API contracts SDK-shaped.
Secrets must not be stored in events; runtime logs, tool artifacts, and provider errors require redaction.
Upstream dependencies are TBD: no accepted dependency edges have been extracted yet.
Downstream dependencies are TBD: no accepted dependency edges have been extracted yet.
Canonicality constraint: events.jsonl remains canonical for runtime replay; SDK transcripts assist resume/debugging but do not displace Chirality events.
Migration constraint: replay must account for both canonical folder sessions and legacy flat session records until migration is explicitly complete.
Exact parser API is TBD: source documents define behavior and storage contracts, not the module API.
Exact transcript view route and UI placement are TBD: sources identify replay/transcript behavior, not a concrete route or component path.
ASSUMPTION: replay should expose compact tool summaries and artifact links rather than raw large payloads, since large payloads are stored as artifacts and referenced by path.
Replay parser must read ordered newline-delimited HarnessEvent records, ignore malformed final records, retain valid prior records, and emit diagnostics for replay/reporting.
Transcript reconstruction groups accepted turns, model deltas/completions, tool lifecycle summaries, and terminal outcomes into a replayable transcript representation.

SDK linkage projection includes sdkSessionId, sdkTranscriptPath or sdkSessionStoreKey, sdkProjectKey, and resume metadata from session metadata when present, while keeping these fields adapter metadata.
Artifact link projection represents large payloads by session artifact paths rather than inlining raw large or sensitive content.

This deliverable makes Chirality runtime work replayable from product-owned records, letting operators and tests reconstruct accepted user turns, assistant output, tool activity summaries, terminal outcomes, diagnostics, artifact references, and SDK transcript linkage.
The replay surface must not treat SDK transcripts or UI state as canonical truth.
Principle: replay from Chirality events first, using events.jsonl as canonical replay input; SDK transcripts aid resume/debugging but do not replace the audit mirror.
Principle: separate UI compactness from audit richness; browser UIEvents stay compact while persisted HarnessEvents may carry richer runtime metadata, and replay must not blur those contracts.
Principle: keep provider-specific details (SDK session IDs, transcript paths, tool names, message names) at adapter boundaries, never as public Chirality contract identity.
Principle: prefer recoverability over all-or-nothing parsing; a malformed trailing JSONL record must not destroy access to earlier valid events.
Principle: do not leak secrets through replay; replay output, diagnostics, and artifact summaries must follow redaction and artifact-reference rules.
The replay model should preserve stable identity fields sessionId, turnId, and event identity, which persist across path and label changes.
Terminal outcomes matter as much as streamed text: accepted turns must end with a durable success, failure, cancellation, or interruption event for reliable replay.
Session metadata can provide SDK linkage (sdkSessionId, sdkTranscriptPath, sdkSessionStoreKey, sdkResumeMode) but replay should present it as linkage metadata, not transcript authority.
Legacy session records remain a compatibility concern until migration is accepted.
The exact view model and API shape are not specified in the source corpus; use TBD for module names, route paths, and component names until implementation ownership is assigned.
Trade-off: favor tolerant replay for a malformed final line while surfacing diagnostics, to protect audit recoverability after interruption or partial writes.
Trade-off: favor compact summaries plus artifact links for large or sensitive tool results, preventing replay views from flooding UI/model context and supporting redaction policy.
Trade-off: show SDK transcript/store linkage as secondary metadata to maintain a provider-neutral core and avoid SDK-shaped public contracts.
Trade-off: keep legacy reads until migration is explicitly complete to preserve existing session usability during layout transition.
For tool results, compact summaries plus artifact references are the preferred replay shape because the audit view needs durable traceability without re-exposing large or sensitive payloads.
Example: a valid event log with accepted turn, model deltas, and completion yields a transcript view showing accepted user input, assistant output, and terminal completion.
Example: an event log with a malformed final line causes replay to ignore the malformed tail, return prior valid events, and surface a diagnostic.
Example: when session metadata includes sdkTranscriptPath, the transcript view may link or display the SDK transcript location as secondary metadata while keeping events.jsonl canonical.
Example: when a tool result event references an artifact, the transcript view should summarize the tool outcome and link the artifact path rather than inlining raw large content.

Step 1 Confirm source contracts: re-read accepted session layout, event schema, replay rules, SDK linkage fields, and browser/runtime contract separation, preserving docs/PRD.md as a warned source if its hash remains mismatched.

Step 2 defines replay input handling: read session.json and events.jsonl for canonical vNext sessions, preserve compatibility for legacy {sessionRoot}/{sessionId}.json until migration closure is accepted, and keep CHIRALITY_SESSION_ROOT override behavior aligned with the session store contract.

Step 3 Parse events.jsonl: process newline-delimited HarnessEvent records in write sequence, validate required event fields, ignore a malformed trailing line while retaining prior valid events, and return or record a diagnostic for malformed-tail replay.

Step 4 Build the transcript projection: group events by turnId where available, project accepted user input, assistant deltas/completions, tool summaries, terminal outcomes, and artifact references, and treat missing optional event categories as absent data rather than parser failure unless a required invariant is violated.
Step 4 ASSUMPTION: expose compact tool summaries and artifact links rather than raw large payloads.

Step 5 Attach SDK transcript linkage: read sdkSessionId, sdkProjectKey, sdkTranscriptPath or sdkSessionStoreKey, sdkConfigDir, and sdkResumeMode when present in session.json, mark them adapter metadata, and never let SDK message names, transcript paths, or session IDs become canonical Chirality identifiers.

Step 6 Apply redaction and safety filtering: ensure replay output and diagnostics do not expose API keys or secret variants, show only summary and artifact reference for large or sensitive tool result data, and surface redaction limitations as diagnostics rather than leaking raw content.

Step 7 Create verification fixtures: valid transcript reconstruction, malformed-tail JSONL, terminal-outcome (success/failure/cancellation/interruption), SDK-linkage confirming events.jsonl canonical, legacy session, redaction, and tool-result artifact-link fixtures, with exact filenames TBD.

Step 8 Run verification: execute unit tests and any Section 9 validation coverage for section9.session_event_replay and section9.sdk_session_link_resume, recording TBD rather than passed when validation IDs are not yet implemented.

Step 9 Record accepted implementation locations: replay parser module path, transcript view model/interface name, route or component placement, and fixture paths, retaining TBD as a handoff blocker rather than inventing a path where unassigned.

DEL-05-04 specifies the backend feature slice reconstructing runtime replay and transcript views from Chirality-owned session events, covering replay parsing, transcript reconstruction tests, malformed-tail handling, terminal-state projection, and SDK transcript linkage as non-canonical adapter metadata.
In scope: read canonical events.jsonl records and session metadata for replay/reporting.
In scope: preserve valid prior JSONL events when the tail line is malformed and surface diagnostics.
In scope: reconstruct accepted turns, assistant output, tool summaries, terminal outcomes, artifact links, and SDK transcript links.
In scope: keep SDK transcripts secondary to Chirality HarnessEvent records unless imported into HarnessEvent form.
In scope: maintain separation between compact browser UIEvents and richer persisted HarnessEvents.
Out of scope: defining the full HarnessEvent schema and append-only writer (primarily DEL-05-02).
Out of scope: canonical session folder migration and legacy session migration helpers (primarily DEL-05-01).
Out of scope: tool result storage thresholds and raw artifact storage (primarily DEL-05-05).
Out of scope: tool permission semantics, excluded by the package context.

DEL-05-04-REQ-002: the replay reader MUST process newline-delimited HarnessEvent records in write sequence.
DEL-05-04-REQ-003: replay MUST ignore a malformed trailing JSONL line, preserve valid prior events, and surface a diagnostic.
DEL-05-04-REQ-004: replay MUST NOT treat SDK transcripts as canonical project or runtime audit truth unless their content has been explicitly imported into HarnessEvent form.
DEL-05-04-REQ-005: transcript reconstruction MUST include accepted user turns and terminal outcomes when the corresponding HarnessEvents are present.

DEL-05-04-REQ-006: transcript reconstruction SHOULD include assistant deltas/completions, tool summaries, artifact links, and SDK transcript links when supported by available events or session metadata.
DEL-05-04-REQ-007: SDK-specific names, IDs, transcript paths, and store keys MUST remain adapter metadata and MUST NOT redefine public Chirality replay contracts.
DEL-05-04-REQ-008: replay output MUST redact or omit secrets and MUST NOT expose API keys from event data, runtime logs, tool artifacts, provider errors, or SDK metadata.
DEL-05-04-REQ-009: legacy session records MUST remain readable for replay-related session discovery until migration completion is explicitly accepted.
DEL-05-04-REQ-010: replay fixtures MUST cover event append/replay, malformed trailing JSONL behavior, and SDK session linkage/resume metadata.
